name: Waldorf Microwave II/XT
description: Waldorf Microwave II, Microwave XT and XTk wavetable synthesizers: every sound parameter of their SysEx specification, sent to the Sound mode edit buffer, with Pull from that edit buffer.

authoringNotes: Generated by tools/profiles/waldorf/make-profiles.mjs; edit the layout in tools/profiles/waldorf/synths/, not this file.
Every parameter is a row of the specification's sound data table, with its printed name. Nothing here has been sent to a real instrument yet.

Sound parameter change: F0 3E 0E <dev> 20 00 <HH> <PP> <value> F7, HH PP the parameter's index (its offset in the sound dump) in two 7-bit bytes, to the Sound mode edit buffer. <dev> is the deviceId variable, the instrument's Device ID (0 unless set otherwise); its dumps are matched by it too.
No identity check: its member code is a bitmask of the hardware fitted (00 00 a Microwave 2, 01 00 one with the XT mainboard, 03 00 a Microwave XT, more with expansions), and a profile takes one.
In Multi mode the same parameter change reaches instrument 1's sound (location 00); the other instruments (01 - 07) are not laid out.
The multi, wave, wavetable, global and display messages are not laid out.

Read through this profile, the sound sets Waldorf publishes for the Microwave II/XT (2,024 sound dumps: factory sets 9712, 9806 and 2000-08, and the user sets beside them) all match the sound dump and pass its checksum. Some hold values the spec does not list, presumably from later system software: modulation destinations 34 and 35 (525 times; the list stops at 33, Mod #4 Amount), Arpeggiator Tempo 0 (469; printed 1 - 127, extern and 50 - 300 BpM), oscillator octaves between the listed steps (136), filter types 10 - 12 (71) and chorus 2 and 3 (48). A Pull of such a sound shows the number.

The dump's checksum is the sound data's sum alone. The spec's dump tables print (BB+NN+SDATA)&7Fh, but its general section says the IDs are not counted, and Waldorf's own factory sounds have the data's sum: 2,000 of 2,017 sound dumps in the Microwave II/XT downloads, the edit buffer dumps among them, and none with the location counted where the two differ. The request sends 7F, which the spec says is always accepted, rather than choose between its (BB+NN) and the 00h its general section gives for a request with no data.
Rows the reader could not split, given by the layout: 84 Panning.
